scenes.title: Cash pressure is a timing problem
scenes.narration: Payroll is approaching. A customer may pay late. A supplier still needs payment. For a small business, those dates can create a cash gap. Probaho helps the owner see that gap, compare realistic options, and stay in control of the next action.
scenes.visual: Opening motion graphic: three dated cards for payroll, receivable, and supplier obligation converge into a timeline. Use product colors; do not use a real-business claim.
on_screen: Cash pressure is a timing problem

scenes.title: Meet Probaho
scenes.narration: Probaho is an SME finance copilot for Topic E. This presentation uses synthetic Bangladeshi taka records in a local sandbox. The workflow is records, projection, comparison, human approval, execution, and evidence.
scenes.visual: Logo/title entrance, then real overview-desktop.png framed as a browser. Small permanent synthetic-sandbox label.

scenes.title: A concrete cash gap
scenes.narration: Shapla Services starts with one hundred twenty thousand taka. Payroll needs eighty thousand, the supplier bill needs seventy thousand, and a confirmed receivable brings twenty thousand. By October thirty-first, closing cash is minus ten thousand. Against a twenty-thousand reserve floor, the shortfall is thirty thousand.
scenes.visual: Zoom through opening-cash metric and source rows in overview-desktop.png. Animate 120,000 + 20,000 − 80,000 − 70,000 = −10,000; reserve shortfall 30,000.

scenes.title: Records with clear scope
scenes.narration: The Records page brings transactions, invoices, and bills together. The owner selects one business and imports a combined CSV. Every row is validated before anything is written. Dates, amounts, currency, and conflicting identifiers are checked, and source records remain linked to the calculations.
scenes.visual: Use records-import.png or recorded Records navigation. Show business selector, transaction/invoice/bill tabs, Import dialog, and sample combined CSV download. Avoid showing a made-up successful import.
on_screen: Validate the whole file before writing

scenes.title: What if the customer pays late?
scenes.narration: The overview compares scheduled cash with a seven-day late-collection scenario. Here, the receivable falls beyond the target date, so closing cash drops to minus thirty thousand and the reserve gap grows to fifty thousand. The arithmetic uses integer paisa, rather than a language model's estimate.
scenes.visual: Crop the Base and Late collection scenario cards from overview-desktop.png. Animate receivable date from Oct 31 to Nov 7 while target remains Oct 31.

scenes.title: Compare recovery options
scenes.narration: Probaho compares a collection reminder, supplier rescheduling, and mock financing. A reminder creates a draft; it never counts as collected cash. Financing shows illustrative fees and repayment terms, but cannot execute. The supplier option proposes deferring forty thousand taka to November seventh, while protecting payroll.
scenes.visual: Use real Recovery plans page from new recording; if unavailable, crop plan-approval.png for actual supplier plan and animate separate faithful option cards. Explicit DRAFT and MOCK labels.

scenes.title: Human review is a separate step
scenes.narration: Before approval, the owner reviews the payee, source bill, amount, dates, assumptions, and policy limits. Approval is a separate human action. Supplier rescheduling also needs a separate acceptance simulation. That button represents a sandbox scenario, not a genuine supplier response.
scenes.visual: Use plan-approval.png. Highlight payee Rahman Supplies, bill-supplier-001, amount 40,000, original date Oct31, deferred date Nov7. Then new live-recording consent panel if available.

scenes.title: Execute once and read it back
scenes.narration: After both gates, execution changes only the synthetic payment schedule. Target-date closing cash becomes thirty thousand taka, with no reserve shortfall. The deferred supplier obligation still exists. A receipt shows the approved action and before-and-after state. Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the original receipt, instead of executing twice.
scenes.visual: Use execution-receipt.png only for fields it truly contains; new recording should show actual approved-recovery card after execution (30,000 closing, 0 shortfall). Show deferred 40,000 obligation at Nov7. Receipt read-back flow.

scenes.title: Evidence and bounded authority
scenes.narration: Plans are bound to the selected business, policy, source records, and sandbox snapshot. Changed details invalidate a pending action. Activity exports include permission events and a per-business hash chain. The assistant has no approval, execution, payment, shell, or SQL tool.
scenes.visual: Motion permission matrix (read/propose allowed; approve/execute human-only) connected to real Activity & evidence recording/export. Hash chain is local evidence, not immutable certification.

scenes.title: An honest assistant mode
scenes.narration: The Assistant can explain the cash gap, project scenarios, compare plans, and draft reminders. The demonstrated mode is labelled Local demo and uses deterministic tools. An optional AI adapter requires the owner's key and per-message consent; live-model quality has not yet been tested.
scenes.visual: Use assistant-demo.png showing Local demo label. Ask “What is the cash gap?” only with real generated answer present. Small provider-status callout.
on_screen: Optional live AI requires key + consent

scenes.title: What has been verified
scenes.narration: Checked-in verification records thirty passing backend tests, eighteen passing deterministic evaluation cases, and desktop and mobile browser checks. These are synthetic correctness and safety results. They do not establish real-world business improvement or production readiness.
scenes.visual: Animated results cards tied to evidence/verification-summary.json; use overview-mobile.png inset. Never label them competition scores or live-AI results.

scenes.title: Keep the owner in control
scenes.narration: Probaho connects a cash gap to a reviewed action and a verifiable receipt. The next step is consented SME usability testing and live-model evaluation. Financial participation, with the owner in control.
scenes.visual: Return to product logo, then single linear workflow and closing phrase. Hold readable end frame.
on_screen: Records → Gap → Plans → Approval → Sandbox → Evidence
